title: Practice 3: Genitive endings: nouns, adjectives, pronouns

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: He returned from Friday prayers.
exercises.why: Similarly, feminine adjectives in the genitive case have the same ending as the prepositional case: **-ой**, or, after the same five 'hush' consonants, **-ей**. *Кило́ хоро́шего ру́сского сы́ра Кило́ хоро́шей ру́сской колбасы́* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.

exercises.q: Разговор начался с ___ (добродушный) подшучиваний, но закончился синяками.
exercises.prompt: The conversation started with friendly banter but ended in bruises.
exercises.why: However, there is a peculiarity in Russian when counting: though we use the genitive singular on nouns that are numbered 2, 3, 4, 22, 23, 24, etc, we use the genitive *plural* for any adjectives attached to that noun: *Три кни́жных магази́на Пять книжных магази́нов Он зна́ет сто два ру́сских сло́ва Он зна́ет сто шесть ру́сских слов* Like nouns, masculine and neuter adjectives have the same ending in the genitive singular, **-ого**, pronounced 'oh-vo'. — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
